text:
marta: quick postmortem note — during canary we saw reads return older kv state after a handoff completed. repro sketch attached. :grimacing:

marta: repro summary:
1) nodeA holds prefix X epoch 42
2) nodeA issues handoff to nodeB (handoff token OPAQUE)
3) nodeB acked ownership, but delayed applying demote/tombstone (GC starving apply)
4) router routed reads to nodeB; nodeB served from a pre-demote snapshot -> stale data

ryan: sounds like the core is that ownership+apply aren't atomic from router's POV. fwiw we have three knobs: change router to wait for explicit applied marker, make apply faster/more reliable, or make reads tolerant to in-flight handoffs (e.g., optimistic read then validate).

cheng: we should avoid adding a synchronous block in the router path if possible. router already contributes to latency. proposal: make handoff produce a durable "apply record" on receiver and expose applied_epoch. router can consult a cheap cache of applied_epoch, defaulting to fallback routing if unknown.

alex: alternative: append-only per-prefix apply-log on receiver. handoff commit = append record {epoch, nonce, tombstone_meta} + fsync. When router sees ownership for epoch E, it requires receiver.applied_epoch >= E. Receiver reads are gated by latest applied epoch in-memory (updated after fsync). This keeps reads cheap but makes handoff commit pay fsync once.

ryan: fsync on every handoff is fine — handoffs are rare relative to reads. but we need correctness across crashes: if receiver restarts it must replay apply-log and restore applied_epoch. keep log small by checkpointing last_applied_epoch in compact manifest periodically.

marta: what about the idempotency surface? retries + duplicates across leader elections are common. each apply record should include a client-provided nonce and server CAS of last_applied_epoch to prevent double-applying. An idempotent API shape: `POST /prefix/:p/apply {epoch, nonce, tombstone}` -> `{applied_epoch, already_applied}`.

cheng: implementation detail: on apply request:
```
lock(prefix)
if nonce in seen_nonce -> return already_applied
if epoch <= last_applied_epoch -> return already_applied
append apply-record; fsync
last_applied_epoch = epoch; mark nonce
unlock
```
This makes it safe to retry and keeps epoch monotonic across crashes.

alex: downside: keeping seen_nonce in memory could grow unbounded. use a tiny LRU persisted window + include epoch in the idempotency key so we expire safely. also emit metric `evict.apply.nonce_conflicts`.

ryan: router changes: when ownership move observed, router asynchronously fetches receiver.applied_epoch; if unknown or < epoch, send to fallback (old owner or proxy) with `X-ownership-stale` header so caller can retry. Only after applied_epoch >= epoch do we route. This avoids blocking critical RPCs.

marta: test plan: unit idempotency, integration with receiver crash during fsync, chaotic test where handoff+fast-evict races under CPU starvation. also add microbenchmark for single-hand off latency (fsync cost) to calibrate.

cheng: telemetry: `handoff.apply.latency_ms` (p50/p95), `handoff.apply.fsync_count`, `handoff.apply.nonce_conflicts`, `handoff.applied_epoch_gap` (router fetch vs observed). Add alert if p95 > 3s in canary.

alex: rollout: feature-flag `handoff_apply_log` default off. phased rollout: canary1 -> canary10 -> canary50 -> prod. also add a compatibility shim: if receiver not supporting apply-log, router uses old behavior (opaque token).

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add feature flag `handoff_apply_log`, schema change: none (api additive), add metrics above, test job `hand off storm` on staging (simulate 500 churn/s), add dashboard and alert.

marta: small UX: make apply API return `applied_epoch` immediately in response when commit completes so calling node can publish to cluster state. Also include `commit_ts` for observability.

ryan: note about performance: we should batch apply records if multiple handoffs for different prefixes target same node in short window; group fsyncs. but batching complicates per-prefix atomicity. maybe group by node but keep per-prefix visibility markers once fsync completes.

cheng: future thought: long-term we could eliminate router fetch by piggybacking applied_epoch onto the cluster membership protocol (a heartbeat that includes per-node high-water marks). tradeoff: metadata size vs realtime accuracy.

alex: I'll draft a small RFC doc summarizing apply-log design, idempotency keys, manifest checkpointing, and router fallback semantics. aim for review today.

marta: I'll produce the canary scenario and the chaos job. schedule sync Friday 11am to sign off.

infra-bot: action items: alex -> rfc draft, cheng -> prototype apply API + small on-disk manifest, ryan -> router fallback + cache, marta -> chaos test + dashboard.

marta: thanks all. this feels lower-risk than a big refactor and gives deterministic safety for handoffs. :white_check_mark:
